title: Customization & Themes
text: dtsmartr features modern, premium dark palette designed clinical environments night shifts. theme = "auto" (Default): Automatically detects browser/system settings matches theme IDE (RStudio Positron). theme = "light": Forces clean light theme. theme = "dark": Forces sleek dark theme.

title: Customization & Themes
text: can enable disable individual layout elements depending context: advanced_filter: Set FALSE hide rule-based Query Builder toolbar. column_picker: Set FALSE remove column dropdown visibility picker top-right toolbar. allow_export: Set FALSE remove clipboard code generator modal button. header_summary: Set FALSE collapse column headers clean, flat labels—removing spark-histograms, top categories bar, missingness progress indicators.

title: Customization & Themes
text: Control missing/null values represented. Cells containing NA null render italicized, muted-gray cells: Default: Displays "NA". Custom: Set na_string = "—" na_string = "Missing" specify custom text.

title: dtsmartr v0.4.0 - API Summary & Programmatic Usage
text: dtsmartr provides interactive, virtualized data explorer widget built React htmlwidgets. offers high-performance data exploration virtual scrolling, multi-column sorting, advanced filtering, column analytics. Key Technologies: - React (via reactR) - Apache Arrow (IPC serialization) - htmlwidgets (R--JavaScript bridge) - Virtual scrolling large datasets

title: dtsmartr v0.4.0 - API Summary & Programmatic Usage
text: Purpose: Create interactive virtualized data grid widget. Signature: Parameters: Behavior: - Auto-detects column types (numeric, character, factor, datetime) - Serializes data Apache Arrow IPC format (Base64) - Extracts column labels attributes (attr(col, "label")) - Auto-routing: Datasets > 50,000 rows automatically redirect dtsmartr_launch() prevent IDE freezing Returns: htmlwidget object (class dtsmartr) Example:
code: dtsmartr(   data,   width         = NULL,   height        = NULL,   elementId     = NULL,   datasetName   = NULL,   options       = dtsmartr_options(),   skip_routing  = FALSE  # Internal - do not use ) library(dtsmartr)  # Basic usage dtsmartr(mtcars)  # With options dtsmartr(   iris,   datasetName = "Iris Dataset",   options = dtsmartr_options(     hidden_columns = c("Species"),     header_density = "minimal",     theme = "dark"   ) )  # Large dataset (auto-routes to external browser) big_data <- data.frame(x = 1:100000, y = rnorm(100000)) dtsmartr(big_data)  # Automatically calls dtsmartr_launch()

title: dtsmartr v0.4.0 - API Summary & Programmatic Usage
text: Purpose: Generate validated configuration options widget. Signature: Parameters: New v0.4.0: - ✨ header_density - Three-mode responsive header compression - ✨ row_density - Adjustable row spacing Returns: Named list validated settings Example:
code: dtsmartr_options(   advanced_filter = TRUE,   show_labels     = TRUE,   column_picker   = TRUE,   allow_export    = TRUE,   theme           = "auto",   na_string       = "NA",   hidden_columns  = NULL,   header_summary  = TRUE,   header_density  = "auto",   row_density     = "standard" ) # Minimal configuration (no analytics) opts_minimal <- dtsmartr_options(   advanced_filter = FALSE,   allow_export    = FALSE,   header_summary  = FALSE,   header_density  = "minimal" )  # Dark theme with hidden columns opts_dark <- dtsmartr_options(   theme          = "dark",   hidden_columns = c("ID", "USUBJID"),   na_string      = "—" )  # Comfortable row spacing opts_comfort <- dtsmartr_options(   row_density = "comfortable" )  # Use with dtsmartr() dtsmartr(mtcars, options = opts_minimal)

what: dtsmartr vs Positron Data Viewer: UI/UX Comparative Analysis
title: dtsmartr vs Positron Data Viewer: UI/UX Comparative Analysis
text: Analyst Role: Principal Software UI/UX Designer specializing IDE data inspection toolsAnalysis Date: July 11, 2026Package Review: dtsmartr v0.3.0Benchmark: Positron Data Viewer (2024-2026 baseline)

title: dtsmartr vs Positron Data Viewer: UI/UX Comparative Analysis
text: comparative analysis evaluates dtsmartr Positron’s native Data Viewer across four design pillars: information density, micro-dashboard architecture, interaction ergonomics, visual hierarchy. analysis based dtsmartr’s documented feature set, QA test results, established UX patterns scientific IDE data viewers. Key Finding: dtsmartr adopts maximalist, analytics-first posture (Kaggle-style inline summaries, sparklines, completeness bars) Positron follows minimalist, spreadsheet-first model (clean grid, metadata demand). valid — optimal choice depends workflow: exploratory data analysis favors dtsmartr’s density; production data inspection favors Positron’s clarity.

title: dtsmartr vs Positron Data Viewer: UI/UX Comparative Analysis
text: Summary: Positron wins speed, minimalism, scale, IDE consistency. dtsmartr wins EDA workflows, metadata discoverability, multi-language export.

title: dtsmartr vs Positron Data Viewer: UI/UX Comparative Analysis
text: dtsmartr better: --glance data profiling: Sparklines (distribution histograms numeric columns, bar charts categorical) missingness progress bars eliminate need open separate summary panels. Reduced cognitive switching: Data scientists can assess column quality (NA%, skewness, cardinality) without leaving grid view. CDISC pharmaceutical readiness: Label attributes appear directly headers, critical clinical trials AVAL vs “Analysis Value (mg/dL)” distinction matters immediately. Use case advantage: exploratory data analysis (EDA), dtsmartr’s headers answer “column usable?” user invests time filtering sorting. Positron alternative: Users must click column → open sidebar → read metadata. faster production work (metadata already known) slower exploration.

title: dtsmartr vs Positron Data Viewer: UI/UX Comparative Analysis
text: dtsmartr better: Multi-condition filtering: Boolean logic (/), comparisons (>, <, ), string patterns (LIKE, regex) single UI. Reproducible queries: Auto-generates R dplyr SQL clauses, exportable notebooks. Use case advantage: Ad-hoc analysis (“show patients AGE > 65 TRTGRP = 'Active' AVAL NULL”) without writing code. Positron alternative: Per-column filters (text box, range slider) faster single-column operations express complex logic without switching console code.

title: dtsmartr vs Positron Data Viewer: UI/UX Comparative Analysis
text: dtsmartr better: Generates R (dplyr) SQL (SELECT ... ) filter/sort operations. Clipboard copy buttons reduce manual translation errors. Use case advantage: Analysts working R+SQL hybrid environments (e.g., R → Postgres pipelines) can validate queries dtsmartr running databases. Positron alternative: R code export . SQL users must manually translate.

title: dtsmartr vs Positron Data Viewer: UI/UX Comparative Analysis
text: dtsmartr better: Drag--freeze animated ⚓ anchor icon provides clear visual feedback. Frozen columns visually distinct (subtle border, lock icon header). Use case advantage: Users discovering feature first time understand immediately (right-click menu exploration required). Positron alternative: Right-click context menu faster experienced users less discoverable new users.
